newsitem.title: UK: BA wants UK to solve French airport dispute.
newsitem.headline: BA wants UK to solve French airport dispute.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday that it hopes the British and French governments can settle its dispute with the French authorities over security at Paris Charles de Gaulle airport.
Earlier this week a Paris court rejected BA's plea for urgent action over its objections to having Algeria's national airline as its new neighbour in the Terminal One check-in hall.
BA has refused to use its check-in when the Algerian desk is open and instead wants to be allowed to transfer all its Paris flights to Orly airport.
BA said the administrative court had postponed judgement for up to two months.
"The case, which was brought on behalf of all airlines operating from Charles De Gaulle, had the full support of the British government," a BA spokesman said.
"We are now looking not only for the French courts but also for discussions between the French and British governments to find a satisfactory solution."

"The case has not been lost," the spokesman said. "All that has been done is that it has been referred to three higher judges for a firm decision and in the meantime we will be looking to the British and French governments to reach a satisfactory solution."
Britain's Department of Transport said government officials would be meeting again next week.
"The British Government shares the concern of British Airways and there will be further consultations between the director-generals of civil aviation for the two governements," a spokeswoman said.

Air Algerie became BA's neighbour last month when it resumed flights to Paris after a break of two years. But BA has refused to check in passengers at the same site or share the same baggage conveyor with Air Algerie for fear of attack by Islamic guerrillas.

The British carrier said on Friday that so far it had had to transfer 8,000 passengers out of a total of 28,000 to other BA flights or other carriers rather than check in their baggage when the Algerian check-in desk is open.
U.S. airline Trans World Airlines has also expressed concern, refusing to park its aircraft at the satellite gate which it shares with the Algerians.
But so far the Paris airports authority has rejected the complaints, insisting that security arrangements for Air Algerie are adequate.
